router_publicly_callable.meaning: TrailsRouter public entry points are callable by anyone

router_funds_nonzero.meaning: router holds nonzero residual ETH and/or ERC20 funds

caller_authorized.meaning: caller is authorized by the router's route logic to move router-held funds

funds_moved_to_arbitrary_target.meaning: router-held residual funds are moved to an arbitrary target outside authorized route logic

assumptions: Public callability is treated as the access-control precondition; the report records this as asserted for TrailsRouter.
Residual non-zero router funds are treated as a possibility, grounded in router_holds_nonzero_funds.
The absence of authorization is grounded in anyone_can_call_without_auth and intent_only_authorized_router_funds.
Either execute or pullAmountAndExecute may be the entry point; the plan remains entry-point agnostic.

unresolved.description: Report does not disambiguate whether execute or pullAmountAndExecute is the primary exploited entry point.
No specific residual fund amount, token, or prior transaction establishing non-zero router balance is given.
Report asserts public callability but does not explicitly state an unauthenticated permissionless caller statement beyond the inferred assumption.

limitations: Only the direct theft of residual router funds impact is formalized for this core claim.
The likely real-world route theft impact is deferred to future claims.
The root cause delegatecall arbitrary transfer is treated as context, not as P or V.
Concrete code/PoC binding and SMT model generation are deferred to the program.
